title: Impact of fermentation by four commercial Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains on substrate and metabolite profiles of dried noni fruit slurry
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Noni (Morinda citrifolia L.) fruit contains bioactive compounds but has a characteristic off-odor associated with medium-chain fatty acids. This study investigated the effects of four commercial Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains (EC1118, 71B, MERIT.ferm, and D47) on substrate utilization and metabolite profiles during fermentation of dried noni fruit slurry (DNFS).

RESULTS

DNFS supplemented with glucose and yeast extract was fermented statically at 25 °C for 4 days. All strains grew from approximately 6 to 7 log CFU mL−1, with D47 reaching 7.14 log CFU mL−1. The total phenolic content showed no significant changes (1.34–1.54 g GAE L−1), whereas DPPH radical-scavenging activity significantly decreased from 56.18% in unfermented DNFS to 36.04–41.84% after fermentation. Vanillic acid increased from 1.64 to 3.51–4.69 mg L−1. Total iridoids showed no significant changes, although MERIT.ferm significantly decreased asperulosidic acid. Volatile profiles were altered, with increases in ethyl esters and higher alcohols and decreases in several aldehydes and furans. EC1118 reduced octanoic and decanoic acids by 20.9% and 30.9%, respectively, whereas D47 produced the largest increase in total esters (40.91 mg L−1).

CONCLUSION

Commercial S. cerevisiae strains produced distinct changes in the metabolite and volatile profiles of DNFS, particularly medium-chain fatty acids and esters. These findings provide a basis for strain selection in further development of fermented DNFS products, although sensory evaluation is needed to determine their effects on aroma perception. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
